graph.summary: Levothyroxine → Triiodothyronine → Thyroid hormone receptor beta → Thyroid hormone mediated signaling pathway → Hypothyroidism

evidence.snippet: The thyroid gland predominantly secretes the pro-hormone thyroxine (T(4)) that is converted to the active hormone 3,5,3'-l-triiodothyronine (T(3)) in target cells.
evidence.explanation: Levothyroxine is synthetic T4; upon administration it is converted to the active metabolite T3 by tissue deiodinases, establishing T3 as its active metabolite.

paper.title: Deiodinases: the balance of thyroid hormone: local control of thyroid hormone action: role of type 2 deiodinase.

evidence.snippet: The monodeiodination of T4 to 3,3',5-triiodothyronine (T3) by selenium-containing deiodinases (ID-1, ID-2) is a key step in the activation of thyroid hormones.
evidence.explanation: Deiodination of T4 to T3 is the key activation step; administered levothyroxine (T4) is therefore a prodrug whose active form is T3.

paper.title: Antithyroid drugs and their analogues: synthesis, structure, and mechanism of action.

evidence.snippet: Thyroid hormone has to be transported into the cell, where it can bind to the thyroid hormone receptor (TR) in the nucleus to exert its effect on cellular gene-transcription.
evidence.explanation: T3 binds nuclear thyroid hormone receptors (including TRβ/THRB) and activates them as transcription factors, directly increasing THRB activity.

paper.title: Thyroid hormone receptors in health and disease.

evidence.snippet: T(3) action in target tissues is determined by DIO2-regulated local availability of T(3) to its nuclear receptors, TRα and TRβ.
evidence.explanation: T3 acts via its nuclear receptors TRα and TRβ (UniProt:P10828); local T3 availability drives receptor activity.

paper.title: Deiodinases: the balance of thyroid hormone: local control of thyroid hormone action: role of type 2 deiodinase.

evidence.snippet: TRβ-deficiency blunts T3-regulated gene expression, indicating that TRβ confers transcriptional sensitivity.
evidence.explanation: TRβ (THRB) is required for T3-regulated gene expression in the pituitary; its deficiency blunts the thyroid hormone mediated signaling pathway.

paper.title: Thyroid hormone-regulated chromatin landscape and transcriptional sensitivity of the pituitary gland.

evidence.snippet: The thyroid hormones act through their nuclear receptor TRs that are T3-modulated transcription factors.
evidence.explanation: TRs including THRB are T3-activated transcription factors that drive thyroid hormone-responsive gene expression, i.e. they positively regulate the thyroid hormone mediated signaling pathway.

paper.title: In Vitro Approaches to Identify Thyroid Hormone Receptor-Dependent Transcriptional Response.

evidence.snippet: optimal therapy for hypothyroidism requires replacement of the deficiency in thyroid hormone with synthetic levothyroxine
evidence.explanation: Hypothyroidism is a state of deficient thyroid hormone signaling; restoring that signaling (via levothyroxine) treats the disease, confirming the pathway negatively regulates the disease state.

paper.title: Evaluation of the therapeutic efficacy of different levothyroxine preparations in the treatment of human thyroid disease.
paper.journal: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association

evidence.snippet: Standard therapy for patients with hypothyroidism is replacement with synthetic thyroxine (T4).
evidence.explanation: Synthetic T4 (levothyroxine) restores thyroid hormone mediated signaling, confirming that active signaling counteracts (negatively regulates) hypothyroidism.

paper.title: Thyroxine alone or thyroxine plus triiodothyronine replacement therapy for hypothyroidism.
